idiom_name: Prisma Json field (Prisma.JsonValue) with connector-specific storage
implementation_notes: In Prisma the entity becomes a Json (or Json?) field in the schema; the client types reads and writes as Prisma.JsonValue and the connector stores the value in the database's JSON-capable column type. Path filters (path plus equals/string_contains and so on) cover the queryable slice on PostgreSQL and MySQL. Because the generated type is open, pair the field with a runtime schema (Zod or similar) - the database will not check the document's shape.
pitfalls: Reads arrive as Prisma.JsonValue, so every payload needs narrowing or validation before it can be used as the entity.
Advanced filters exist only on PostgreSQL and MySQL, and the path syntax differs per connector (array form versus $.key), so query code is less portable than the column type suggests.
No relations, indexes or constraints reach inside the document, so the model can drift silently from what the application expects.
